Command: Reprove your neighbour rather than bearing sin for him
Summary: One of the neighbour-laws of Leviticus 19:17-18: reprove your neighbour rather than bearing sin for him, part of the passage that ends in 'thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.'
Commandment: Reprove your neighbour rather than bearing sin for him
Application: Jesus joins this neighbour rule to love of God as the hinge of the Law (Matthew 22:39-40); love of neighbour is the measure of love of God in practice.
Purpose: Leviticus 19:18 states the neighbor rule; Jesus joins it to love of God as the hinge of the Law (Matthew 22:39-40).
Function: This law names a duty that does not expire: it is about character, not procedure. One of the neighbour-laws of Leviticus 19:17-18: reprove your neighbour rather than bearing sin for him. Leviticus 19:18 states the neighbor rule; Jesus joins it to love of God as the hinge of the Law. The command itself does the work: reprove your neighbour rather than bearing sin for him.
